title: Morning Breaks upon the Tomb
description: Morning Breaks upon the Tomb in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Bengo Collyer wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 236 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Morn-ing breaks up-on the tomb! Je-sus dis-si-pates its gloom! Day of tri-umph through the skies, See the glo-rious Sa-viour rise!

lines: Day of triumph through the skies,
Doubt no more his power to save.
Ye who are of death afraid,
See the place where Jesus lay.
Chase the terrors of the night.

licence: Public domain: William Bengo Collyer died in 1854.
credits: Words by William Bengo Collyer (1782–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
